title: Annotatio IV §.I close: Scripture true — Caro mea / Paul communion; stop before §.II (John 6 & Paul on mode)
pass_a_gloss: For whatever Holy Scripture teaches, that ought to be true and undoubted for us. Therefore it must be confessed true and no less undoubted what Christ said: My flesh is truly food and my blood is drink; which according to blessed Paul are communicated to us through bread and cup: for he called the same bread the communion of Christ’s body, and likewise the cup the cup of His blood.
pass_b_english: Whatever Holy Scripture teaches must be true and undoubted for us — so also Christ’s My flesh is truly food and my blood drink, communicated through bread and cup per Paul.
Paul called the bread the communion of Christ’s body and the cup the cup of His blood.
Stop before §.II (John 6 and Paul as the mode-commentaries on Institution).
source_text: Quicquid enim sacrosancta docet Scriptura, id nobis verum ac indubitatum esse oportet. Verum igitur nec minùs indubium esse fatendum est, quod dixit Christus: Caro mea verè est cibus & sanguis meus est potus; quæ juxta B. Paulum per panem & poculum nobis communicantur: eundem enim panem communionem corporis Christi, itidemque poculum, sanguinis ipsius poculum, appellavit.
